brief.name: Lantern Drift
brief.category: Casual puzzle game (mobile, iOS and Android)
brief.pitch: Rotate paper tiles so a thread of light connects every lantern on the board, then watch the lanterns float up into the dusk.
mechanics: Tap a tile to rotate it
Link light paths across the board
brief.art_style: Warm paper-cut dusk with layered paper, soft grain, and no realistic humans
brief.tone: Calm, cozy, and a little clever
facts: A new daily board is available
brief.launch_goal: Drive installs from casual puzzle players through Meta, TikTok, and Google UAC during a global soft launch.

concepts.audience_note: Players who want a reliable way to fill short gaps on trains, flights, and in queues, often with patchy or no connection. They care most about a game that is ready whenever they are.
concepts.angle: Offer a cozy, calm mood as a contrast to the stress of a crowded commute or a long wait.
concepts.hook_line: Trade commute stress for cozy calm.

meta.headline: Trade commute stress for cozy calm.
meta.text: Rotate paper tiles, link a thread of light, and watch lanterns drift up into the dusk. Levels take about 3 minutes.

tiktok.headline: Trade commute stress for calm
tiktok.text: Link a thread of light and send lanterns up into the dusk. Calm, cozy, about 3 minutes a level.

google_uac.headline: Cozy calm for your commute
google_uac.text: Link light across paper tiles and watch lanterns float up. About 3 minutes a level.

art.image_prompt: Layered paper cut-out scene of a warm dusk sky in deep indigo #1B1F4B fading to amber #FFB547 at the horizon, with a large glowing paper orb like a setting sun at the center. Concentric rings of cream #FFF1D6 paper form soft ridges around it. Floating paper lanterns in coral #E8556D and amber drift at different depths, and glowing amber light threads loop gently around the orb like calm ripples. Soft film grain, subtle paper edge shadows, and a tactile handmade feel. Quiet, cozy, and spacious, with an empty calm area of dark indigo sky in the upper third. No people, no text. Style tokens: layered paper cut-outs; soft film grain; warm dusk glow; glowing amber light threads; floating paper lanterns.

critic.policy_notes: The image has no real-money, prize, or multiplayer implications, and no humans, stats, or shouting. The 'Play Now' pill is a flat graphic CTA inside the ad creative. It could read as a clickable button, which is a minor fake-UI risk, though it is a common ad convention. The concentric dashed rings with orbiting dots are abstract and show no specific mechanics, so nothing is misleading. The image also does not mention any true facts such as free to play, offline, or no timers.
critic.summary: The ad is clean and highly legible, with a clear CTA and a calm dusk mood that supports the cozy-calm headline. However, it reads as flat vector gradients rather than layered paper-cut with grain, and it has no lantern or commute cue, so brand fit and message match are only moderate.

art.image_prompt: Close, slightly angled view of a grid of chunky layered paper-cut tiles in cream #FFF1D6, amber #FFB547, coral #E8556D, and indigo #1B1F4B. Each tile carries a simple cut-out pattern of paper lines. One tile in the middle is mid-rotation, tilted at a playful angle, with glowing amber light threads connecting its pattern to neighboring tiles. A few small floating paper lanterns hover above the grid in a warm dusk glow. Soft film grain, visible paper fibers, gentle drop shadows between layers, and an indigo dusk background. Leave generous empty space at the bottom of the frame. No people, no hands, no text. Style tokens: layered paper cut-outs; soft film grain; warm dusk glow; glowing amber light threads; floating paper lanterns.

critic.text_read: Tap a tile and play Play Now
critic.policy_notes: The 'Play Now' pill is drawn inside the ad image, so it looks like a clickable UI element but is not one. That is a fake-button risk, and the policy risk is moderate. The grid of tiles with clock-like hands implies a tile-tapping puzzle. That may not match the real Lantern Drift mechanics, and the clock faces could suggest time pressure, even though levels have no timers. No prize, multiplayer or human content is implied. No false claims are made in the text. The image text 'Tap a tile and play' largely repeats the headline 'Tap a tile. You're already playing.'
critic.summary: The ad is clean and readable with strong contrast on the CTA and headline, but the in-image 'Play Now' button is a fake UI element, the clock-like tile grid may misrepresent gameplay or imply timers, and the flat vector look with brown tiles departs from the layered paper-cut dusk style and its amber/cream/coral palette, so the ad only partly fits the brand and the headline.
critic.intended_text: Tap a tile and play Play Now

art.image_prompt: A close-up grid of layered paper-cut tiles in deep indigo #1B1F4B and cream #FFF1D6, each tile slightly rotated at a different angle. A few tiles are aligned, and glowing amber #FFB547 light threads run through them to connect the pattern. Small coral #E8556D paper accents sit on the edges. A few small floating paper lanterns drift at the edges of the frame. Warm dusk glow, soft film grain, and gentle shadows between the paper layers give depth. The composition is calm and uncluttered, with a quiet empty band of dusk sky across the lower third. Style tokens: layered paper cut-outs; soft film grain; warm dusk glow; glowing amber light threads; floating paper lanterns.

critic.policy_notes: The 'Play Now' pill looks like a real button, but it works as a standard ad CTA and is a minor concern at most. The grid of rotating clock-hand tiles seems to illustrate the tap-to-turn mechanic with no prizes, chat, multiplayer, or combat implied, though it may not match the real gameplay of Lantern Drift. The on-image text 'Tap turn glow' omits the commas and the 'Repeat softly' line from the headline, and it reads slightly awkwardly as a command. The cropped grid at the bottom edge could pass as a live game screen, so the image should reflect actual in-game visuals. Nothing mentions timers, so there is no contradiction with the no-timer fact. There are no unsourced stats and no shouting.
critic.summary: A clean, high-contrast ad with a clear CTA and a tap-and-turn tile grid that supports the headline, but the style drifts from the paper-cut dusk look (flat vector, brown tiles, no lanterns or grain, and the amber #FFB547 is missing), the card overlaps the grid awkwardly, and the shown mechanic may not match real gameplay.
